4.10 Project Plan and Implementation Methodology 
The project will be implemented using a hybrid between waterfall and agile 
methodologies, this decision allows for the structured research and development 
phases, while also providing the flexibility to revisit and refine earlier stages of 
the projects lifecycle as new information is uncovered. This approach is 
particularly benefitable, due to challenges regarding DBS checks, making regular 
client visitations unfeasible throughout the project. By utilising this development 
strategy, the project will maintain a clear structured path, while remaining 
adaptable to new insights and enhancements. 
The project will be divided into subatomic tasks, that will be ordered by priority 
as defined in Table 5 and Table 6. The developer is expected to complete these 
tasks in a sequential order, guaranteeing that given the worst case scenario that 
development is halted prematurely the best version of the product is released at 
any one time. The entire development portion of the project is estimated to take 
a significant portion of the projects allocated 400 hours, at around 231 hours 
(excluding redundancy periods), making this highest-priority first approach all 
the more critical to the project’s success.
